context: The original sorted array has no duplicates: nums = [1, 3, 6, 8, 12, 15, 23, 26, 31, 35]. The value to insert is target = 6. The array must remain sorted. If it already contains an element equal to target, insert the new element to the left of the equal element.
description: The top row shows the original array nums. An upward arrow labeled “Insertion point” marks the gap between 3 at index 1 and the existing 6 at index 2. The insertion index for target is 2.

A thick downward arrow labeled “Insert target” leads to the lower row, which shows the 11-element array after insertion: [1, 3, 6, 6, 8, 12, 15, 23, 26, 31, 35]. The newly inserted 6, highlighted in teal, occupies index 2. The original green 6 and all elements to its right shift one position to the right, putting the original 6 at index 3.

frames.explanation: The initial array here has no duplicates, so the existing target marks the insertion point. After insertion, equal elements are allowed.
frames.title: Insertion point in a sorted array

summary: Insert a new value to the left of an equal element to keep the array sorted.
title: Insertion point in a sorted array
